text:
alex: heads-up — POC with Acme edge site (APAC rack) is blocked. They pinned model="gptx-3.2" in the deploy config but inference fails with model compatibility errors on their ARM boxes. Can we swarm?

jordan: @alex can you paste the error payload? is this during download or runtime?

alex: it's runtime. customer saw a 503 and this in container logs: 
```
ERROR: model_load_failed: incompatible-arch: binary not supported on aarch64
model: gptx-3.2
variant: float16
required: x86_64
```

maria: that looks like our standard mismatch — the pinned artifact for gptx-3.2 defaulted to an x86 build. Edge/arm customers need the -armv8 or q4 quantized build.

chris: quick workaround: point them at model_alias "gptx-3.2-armv8-q4" or set runtime.fallback_to_compatible = true in the POC config so the control plane can serve a compatible variant. Example patch: 
```yaml
model_pin: gptx-3.2-armv8-q4
policies:
  allow_variant_fallback: true
```

alex: client is worried about output quality with q4 quant. also asked about pricing impact if we switch to a compatible variant or to hosted.

jordan: q4 will shave cost but may slightly change tokens-perplexity. For POC we usually recommend enabling fallback + side-by-side eval. I can run an eval on their prompt set quickly.

maria: from infra side, enabling fallback is safe; it routes to a compatible artifact. If they need strict pinning for reproducibility, we have two options: 1) provision a dedicated x86 Dedicated node in APAC (higher cost) 2) re-pin to an arm-compatible model build and note quantization variance.

deploy-bot: [system] artifact-resolver: attempted fetch -> /models/gptx-3.2/x86_64/v1 -> 404
deploy-bot: [system] artifact-resolver: searched compatible variants -> /models/gptx-3.2/armv8/q4/v1 -> found

chris: if they want to keep exact weights (no quant), we'd need to move to Dedicated or Private so we can host the x86 binary in their VPC/edge proxy. That triggers a pricing bump — Jordan, can you flag pricing?

jordan: noted. I'll prepare a short price delta: Dedicated monthly add-on vs hosted fallback. Also add a note for support hours to assist with evals.

alex: customer also dropped a security questionnaire asking about KMS/HSM for keys on edge. Is that supported for Private?

maria: yes — Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. For edge sites we usually ship a tiny control-plane adapter that talks to their KMS over mTLS. I'll queue a short runbook.

chris: longer term: we'll prod model onboarding to publish an explicit compatibility matrix per artifact (arch, quant, kernel). For now, immediate steps:
- Jordan: send pricing delta + decision options to Acme (fallback vs Dedicated vs re-pin)
- Alex: enable allow_variant_fallback on the POC tenant and share prompt set with Jordan
- Maria: share edge KMS runbook + confirm network requirements
- Chris: if they pick strict pin to x86, we'll schedule a Private/Dedicated onboarding call

alex: doing that now. Thanks everyone — will update once customer decides. :thumbsup:

jordan: I'll draft email and attach quick eval plan. ETA 2 hours.

maria: ping me if you need the runbook earlier, I can drop the doc link here.

alex: resolved-for-now — fallback enabled and customer running smoke tests. will reopen thread if any regressions.

chris: created follow-up ticket INF-5421 to track compatibility matrix work and edge model artifacts.
